q: The capacitance of a capacitor is $100\,\mu\text{F}$, and it is charged to a voltage of $12\,\text{V}$. How large is its charge?
Why does the energy of a capacitor $W = \tfrac{1}{2} Q U$ have the factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$?
a: In charging the voltage grows from zero to $U$ in the same proportion as the charge. The first charges move across a small voltage and the last across the whole voltage, so the average voltage is $\tfrac{U}{2}$. The energy is the area of the triangle under the $(Q, U)$ graph.
